				<article id="post-29057" class="post-29057 page type-page status-publish hentry">

				
					<div class="entry-content">
					<div class="et-l et-l--post">
			<div class="et_builder_inner_content et_pb_gutters3">
		<div class="et_pb_section et_pb_section_0 et_pb_with_background et_section_regular" data-padding="0px|0px|0px|0px" >
				
				
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_row et_pb_row_0 et_pb_row_fullwidth et_pb_gutters1">
				<div class="et_pb_column et_pb_column_4_4 et_pb_column_0  et_pb_css_mix_blend_mode_passthrough et-last-child">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_module et_pb_text et_pb_text_0  et_pb_text_align_center et_pb_bg_layout_dark">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_text_inner"><h1>Wild North Downwind Route</h1>
<p>Downwinds from Tatajuba to Atins</p></div>
			</div>
			</div>
				
				
				
				
			</div><div class="et_pb_row et_pb_row_1 et_pb_row_fullwidth et_pb_gutters1">
				<div class="et_pb_column et_pb_column_2_3 et_pb_column_1  et_pb_css_mix_blend_mode_passthrough">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_module et_pb_text et_pb_text_1  et_pb_text_align_left et_pb_bg_layout_light">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_text_inner"><p style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 15pt;"><strong><span style="font-family: Gloria Hallelujah; letter-spacing: 0px; line-height: 1em; font-transform: uppercase; color: #063347;">Exploring the Wild North – 13 days (11 days of kiting + 2 days of transfers)</span><br /></strong></span></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">On this <strong>downwinder</strong> you will kite along the coastlines of 3 entirely different states; <strong>Ceará, Piaui</strong> and <strong>Maranhão</strong>. You’ll cover around 240km where you will cross deserted beaches, lagoons, river mouths and terrific wave spots. You’ll enter the <strong>Delta of Parnaiba</strong>, the biggest delta in the America along with its infinite chain of islands and perfect flat waters, finishing the trip in one of the best and most stunning dune parks in the world, the Lençóis Maranhenses National Park, with its endless crystal clear-water lagoons.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">Picture yourself doing these downwinds with a view of isolated beaches, dunes and natural beauty. You’ll feel completely integrated in beauty and nature. </p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">The pit stops are strategic with 2 nights minimum each in place allowing time not only to rest, but also to really get to know each village well, along with its people and all the different kite spots it has to offer.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">Without a doubt, you will never experience anything quite like this. Traveling along this part of the <strong>coast in the north Brazil</strong> by kite will be an adventure like no other.</p></div>
			</div><div class="et_pb_module et_pb_text et_pb_text_2  et_pb_text_align_left et_pb_bg_layout_light">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_text_inner"><p style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 15pt;"><strong><span style="font-family: Gloria Hallelujah; letter-spacing: 0px; line-height: 1em; font-transform: uppercase; color: #063347;">13 days (11 days of kiting + 2 days of transfers)</span><br /></strong></span></p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">On this <strong>downwinder</strong> you will kite along the coastlines of 3 entirely different states; <strong>Ceará</strong>, <strong>Piaui</strong> and <strong>Maranhão</strong>. You’ll cover around 240km where you will cross deserted beaches, lagoons, river mouths and terrific wave spots. You’ll enter the <strong>Delta of Parnaiba</strong>, the biggest delta in the America along with its infinite chain of islands and perfect flat waters, finishing the trip in one of the best and most stunning dune parks in the world, the Lençóis Maranhenses National Park, with its endless crystal clear-water lagoons.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">Picture yourself doing these downwinds with a view of isolated beaches, dunes and natural beauty. You’ll feel completely integrated in beauty and nature. </p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">The pit stops are strategic with 2 nights minimum each in place allowing time not only to rest, but also to really get to know each village well, along with its people and all the different kite spots it has to offer.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">Without a doubt, you will never experience anything quite like this. Traveling along this part of the <strong>coast in the north Brazil</strong> by kite will be an adventure like no other.</p></div>
			</div>
			</div><div class="et_pb_column et_pb_column_1_3 et_pb_column_2  et_pb_css_mix_blend_mode_passthrough et-last-child">

				<div class="et_pb_with_border et_pb_module et_pb_blurb et_pb_blurb_0  et_pb_text_align_center  et_pb_blurb_position_top et_pb_bg_layout_light">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_blurb_content">
					<div class="et_pb_main_blurb_image"><span class="et_pb_image_wrap et_pb_only_image_mode_wrap"><img decoding="async" width="167" height="150" src="https://www.freeridekitesurf.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/palmera_167x150.png" alt="downwind kite safari Taiba Jericoacoara" class="et-waypoint et_pb_animation_top et_pb_animation_top_tablet et_pb_animation_top_phone wp-image-27719" /></span></div>
					<div class="et_pb_blurb_container">
						<h4 class="et_pb_module_header"><span>Wind (Knots)</span></h4>
						<div class="et_pb_blurb_description"><p>18kn – 35 kn depending on the different spots.</p>
<p>Probability of wind – 95%</p></div>
					</div>
				</div>
			</div>
			</div><div class="et_pb_column et_pb_column_1_3 et_pb_column_4  et_pb_css_mix_blend_mode_passthrough">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_with_border et_pb_module et_pb_blurb et_pb_blurb_1  et_pb_text_align_center  et_pb_blurb_position_top et_pb_bg_layout_light">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_blurb_content">
					<div class="et_pb_main_blurb_image"><span class="et_pb_image_wrap et_pb_only_image_mode_wrap"><img decoding="async" width="150" height="150" src="https://www.freeridekitesurf.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/kitesize_150x150.png" alt="downwind kite safari Taiba Jericoacoara" class="et-waypoint et_pb_animation_top et_pb_animation_top_tablet et_pb_animation_top_phone wp-image-27715" /></span></div>
					<div class="et_pb_blurb_container">
						<h4 class="et_pb_module_header"><span>Kite Size</span></h4>
						<div class="et_pb_blurb_description"><p>Men (take 2 sizes): 8 &amp; 11 depending on weight</p>
<p>Women (take 2 sizes) : 6 &amp; 9 depending on weight</p></div>
					</div>
				</div>
			</div>
			</div><div class="et_pb_column et_pb_column_1_3 et_pb_column_5  et_pb_css_mix_blend_mode_passthrough et-last-child">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_with_border et_pb_module et_pb_blurb et_pb_blurb_2  et_pb_text_align_center  et_pb_blurb_position_top et_pb_bg_layout_light">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_blurb_content">
					<div class="et_pb_main_blurb_image"><span class="et_pb_image_wrap et_pb_only_image_mode_wrap"><img decoding="async" width="150" height="150" src="https://www.freeridekitesurf.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/temperature_150x150.png" alt="downwind kite safari Taiba Jericoacoara" class="et-waypoint et_pb_animation_top et_pb_animation_top_tablet et_pb_animation_top_phone wp-image-27723" /></span></div>
					<div class="et_pb_blurb_container">
						<h4 class="et_pb_module_header"><span>Weather</span></h4>
						<div class="et_pb_blurb_description"><p>Air temperature 28˚C – 38˚C all year round</p>
<p>Water temperature 26˚C – 28˚C all year round</p></div>
					</div>
				</div>
			</div>
			</div>
				
				
				
				
			</div>
				
				
			</div><div class="et_pb_section et_pb_section_1 et_pb_with_background et_section_regular" >
				
				
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_with_border et_pb_row et_pb_row_3 et_pb_row_fullwidth et_pb_gutters1">
				<div class="et_pb_column et_pb_column_1_2 et_pb_column_6  et_pb_css_mix_blend_mode_passthrough">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_with_border et_pb_module et_pb_text et_pb_text_3  et_pb_text_align_left et_pb_bg_layout_dark">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_text_inner"><p style="text-align: center; font-size: 25px;"><strong><span style="text-decoration: underline;">PROGRAM</span></strong></p>
<p style="text-align: left;"><strong>DAY 1:</strong> Transfer in 4×4 Cumbuco – Tatajuba (5h aprox).<br /><strong>DAY 2:</strong> Downwind Tatajuba &#8211; Praia de Maceió (Camocim) &#8211; 35km -&gt; 4&#215;4 to Barra Grande<br /><strong>DAY 3:</strong> Kite in Lagoa do Mangue &amp; Macapá<br /><strong>DAY 4:</strong> Downwind Barra Grande to Aimbere Resort &#8211; 25km<br /><strong>DAY 5:</strong> Downwind Pedra do Sal to Pontal (20km)<br /><strong>DAY 6:</strong> Downwind Pontal – Ilha do Cajú &#8211; 35km<br /><strong>DAY 7:</strong> Downwind Ilha do Cajú – Arpoador 50km<br /><strong>DAY 8:</strong> Kite in Arpoador<br /><strong>DAY 9:</strong> Downwind Arpoador – Atins &#8211; 65km<br /><strong>DAY 10:</strong> Downwind to Canto do Atins (15km) &#8211; kite in the lagoons of the Lençois Maranhenses National Park<br /><strong>DAY 11:</strong> Kite in Atins<br /><strong>DAY 12:</strong> Transfer 4&#215;4 Atins to Praia do Maceió &#8211; kite in the afternoon<br /><strong>DAY 13:</strong> Transfer Praia de Maceió to Fortaleza airport</p></div>
			</div>
			</div><div class="et_pb_column et_pb_column_1_2 et_pb_column_7  et_pb_css_mix_blend_mode_passthrough et-last-child">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_module et_pb_text et_pb_text_4  et_pb_text_align_left et_pb_bg_layout_dark">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_text_inner"><p style="text-align: justify;">This Kite Safari is <strong>limited to a maximum of 12 people</strong> and a <strong>minimum of 3</strong>. There will always be 1 or 2 guides in the water depending on the size of group.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">It’s important to note that during the downwinds in this trip, the 4x4s won’t be able to follow the group along the beach at all times, mainly because vehicles are not allowed along the coastline of the State of Piauí. This is why for this trip we require all riders to have at least a high intermmediate level, if not advanced. Guides are there not only to lead the group, but also to ensure the safety of the group during the downwinds. If they believe there’s anyone who hasn’t have the necessary skills to ride along some advanced parts of the downwind, this person will have to go in the 4×4 during these parts for his own safety and the group’s as well.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">We recommend you bring 2 different sized kites, 2 bars and 2 boards. To repair any type of material can be fairly complicated for the most part which is why we recommend bringing extra to avoid these types of situations. Also, one should bear in mind that being close to the equator, the sun is very strong so a good quality water proof sunscreen is a must. Zinc works very well. Sunglasses, long sleeve with UV protection and a hat is always a good idea.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">If you’re a group of at least 3 friends, it is possible to personalize this trip for you by staying more or less days in each place. All you would have to do is let us know how you would like your Kite Safari to be and we will make it happen.</p></div>
			</div>
			</div>
				
				
				
				
			</div>
				
				
			</div><div class="et_pb_section et_pb_section_2 et_pb_with_background et_section_regular" >

				<div class="et_pb_text_inner"><p style="text-align: center; font-size: 21px;"><strong><span style="text-decoration: underline;">PROGRAM</span></strong></p>
<p style="text-align: left;"><strong>DAY 1:</strong> Transfer in 4×4 Cumbuco – Tatajuba (5h aprox).<br /><strong>DAY 2:</strong> Downwind Tatajuba &#8211; Praia de Maceió (Camocim) &#8211; 35km -&gt; 4&#215;4 to Barra Grande<br /><strong>DAY 3:</strong> Kite in Lagoa do Mangue &amp; Macapá<br /><strong>DAY 4:</strong> Downwind Barra Grande to Aimbere Resort &#8211; 25km<br /><strong>DAY 5:</strong> Downwind Pedra do Sal to Pontal (20km)<br /><strong>DAY 6:</strong> Downwind Pontal – Ilha do Cajú &#8211; 35km<br /><strong>DAY 7:</strong> Downwind Ilha do Cajú – Arpoador 50km<br /><strong>DAY 8:</strong> Kite in Arpoador<br /><strong>DAY 9:</strong> Downwind Arpoador – Atins &#8211; 65km<br /><strong>DAY 10:</strong> Downwind to Canto do Atins (15km) &#8211; kite in the lagoons of the Lençois Maranhenses National Park<br /><strong>DAY 11:</strong> Kite in Atins<br /><strong>DAY 12:</strong> Transfer 4&#215;4 Atins to Praia do Maceió &#8211; kite in the afternoon<br /><strong>DAY 13:</strong> Transfer Praia de Maceió to Fortaleza airport</p></div>
			</div>
			</div><div class="et_pb_column et_pb_column_1_2 et_pb_column_9  et_pb_css_mix_blend_mode_passthrough et-last-child">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_module et_pb_text et_pb_text_6  et_pb_text_align_left et_pb_bg_layout_dark">
				
				
				
				
				<div class="et_pb_text_inner"><p style="text-align: justify;">This Kite Safari is <strong>limited to a maximum of 12 people</strong> and a <strong>minimum of 3</strong>. There will always be 1 or 2 guides in the water depending on the size of group.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">It’s important to note that during the downwinds in this trip, the 4x4s won’t be able to follow the group along the beach at all times, mainly because vehicles are not allowed along the coastline of the State of Piauí. This is why for this trip we require all riders to have at least a high intermmediate level, if not advanced. Guides are there not only to lead the group, but also to ensure the safety of the group during the downwinds. If they believe there’s anyone who hasn’t have the necessary skills to ride along some advanced parts of the downwind, this person will have to go in the 4×4 during these parts for his own safety and the group’s as well.</p>
<p style="text-align: justify;">We recommend you bring 2 different sized kites, 2 bars and 2 boards. To repair any type of material can be fairly complicated for the most part which is why we recommend bringing extra to avoid these types of situations. Also, one should bear in mind that being close to the equator, the sun is very strong so a good quality water proof sunscreen is a must. Zinc works very well. Sunglasses, long sleeve with UV protection and a hat is always a good idea.</p>
